The families of dynamically (central) syndetic, dynamically thick (sets of pointwise recurrence), and dynamically (central) piecewise syndetic sets are denoted by     (   ),     (   ), and     (   ), respectively. The acronym ``SIF'' stands for ``syndetic, idempotent filter.''

Theorem 3.15: tabular c Combinatorial char of membership in SIF tabular
nodes.statement:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item 
        If $A$ is central syndetic and $\mathscr{F}$ is a syndetic, idempotent filter to which $A$ belongs, then the set $A \cap (A-\mathscr{F})$ satisfies the condition in (3.6).

        \item 
        If $A$ satisfies the condition in (3.6), then the family
        \[\mathscr{F} \vcentcolon= \big\uparrow \bigg\{ A \cap \bigcap_{f \in F} (A - f) \ \bigg | \ F \subseteq A \text{ is finite} \bigg\}\]
        is a syndetic, idempotent filter that contains $A$, whereby $A$ is central syndetic.
    \end{enumerate}
    In particular, the set $A$ is central syndetic if and only if some subset of it satisfies the condition in (3.6).

nodes.name: Theorem 3.13: tabular c $A$ in SIF $H$ thick implies $A \cap H$ is central tabular
nodes.statement: Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be central syndetic.  For all minimal left ideals $L \subseteq \beta \mathbb{N}$, there exists an idempotent $p \in L$ such that $A \in p$.  In particular, for all thick sets $H \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, the set $A \cap H$ is central.

nodes.name: Theorem E: tabular c Partitioning $dc\mathcal{S}$ sets tabular
nodes.statement: Every dynamically central syndetic set can be partitioned into infinitely many, pairwise disjoint dynamically central syndetic sets.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.18: tabular c $dc\mathcal{S}$ iff member of SIF tabular
nodes.statement: A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is dynamically central syndetic if and only if it is central syndetic, that is, a member of a syndetic, idempotent filter on $\mathbb{N}$.

nodes.statement: If $\mathscr{F}$ is a syndetic, idempotent filter and $\mathscr{G}$ is a $\mathcal{C}^*$, idempotent filter, then $\mathscr{F} \sqcap \mathscr{G}$ is a syndetic, idempotent filter.

nodes.statement: There exist sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that are not sets of pointwise recurrence but for which $\mathbb{N} = A \cup B$.  In particular, the family of sets of pointwise recurrence is not partition regular.

nodes.name: Theorem A, Theorem B: tabular c Characterizations of $d\mathcal{S}$ $dc\mathcal{S}$ tabular
nodes.statement:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$.  The following are equivalent.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item
        
        The set $A$ is dynamically syndetic.

        \item
        
        There exists a nonempty subset $B \subseteq A$ that satisfies: for all finite $F \subseteq B$, the set $\bigcap_{f \in F} (B-f)$ is syndetic.

        \item
        
        There exists $n \in \mathbb{N}$ for which the set $A - n$ belongs to a syndetic, idempotent filter on $\mathbb{N}$.
    \end{enumerate}

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$.  The following are equivalent.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item 
        The set $A$ is dynamically central syndetic.

        \item 
        There exists a subset $B \subseteq A$ that satisfies: for all finite $F \subseteq B$, the set $B \cap \bigcap_{f \in F} (B-f)$ is syndetic.

        \item 
        The set $A$ belongs to a syndetic, idempotent filter on $\mathbb{N}$.
    \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Theorem 5.8: tabular c $\mathcal{C}^*$ idempotent filters $\subseteq dc\mathcal{PS}^*$ Syndetic t -i…
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathscr{G}$ be a filter on $\mathbb{N}$.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item
    
    If $\mathscr{G}$ is a $\mathcal{C}^*$, idempotent filter, then $\mathscr{G} \subseteq dc\mathcal{PS}^*$.

    \item
    
    If $\mathscr{G}$ is a syndetic, translation-invariant filter, then $\mathscr{G} \subseteq d\mathcal{PS}^*$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.statement: Let $(X,T)$ be a not-necessarily-metrizable, minimal topological dynamical system.  For all $x \in X$ and all nonempty, open $U \subseteq X$ (containing $x$), the set $R(x,U)$ is dynamically (central) syndetic.

nodes.statement:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$.  The following are equivalent.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item
        
        $A$ is a set of pointwise recurrence.

        \item
        
        For all $B \supseteq A$, there exists a finite set $F \subseteq \mathbb{N} \backslash B$ such that the set $B \cup \big( B-F \big)$ is thick.

        \item
        
        For all syndetic $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, there exists a finite set $F \subseteq A$ such that for all syndetic $S' \subseteq S$,
        \[F \cap (S - S') \neq \emptyset.\]
    \end{enumerate}

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$.  The following are equivalent.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item 
        
        $A$ is dynamically thick.

        \item 
        
        For all $\mathbb{N} \supsetneq B \supseteq A$, there exists a finite set $F \subseteq \mathbb{N} \backslash B$ such that the set $B-F$ is thick.

        \item 
        For all piecewise syndetic $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, there exists a finite set $F \subseteq A$ such that the set $S-F$ is thick.
    \end{enumerate}

nodes.statement: Dynamically central piecewise syndetic sets are sets of polynomial multiple measurable recurrence for commuting transformations.

nodes.statement: The family of dynamically (central) piecewise syndetic sets is (properly) contained the family of piecewise syndetic sets, ie., $dc\mathcal{PS} \subsetneq \mathcal{PS}$ and $d\mathcal{PS} \subseteq \mathcal{PS}$.

Theorem G: tabular c $\mathcal{C} \subsetneq dc\mathcal{PS} \subsetneq d\mathcal{PS} = \mathcal{PS}$…
nodes.statement:
Denote by $\mathcal{C}$, $\mathcal{PS}$, $d\mathcal{PS}$, and $dc\mathcal{PS}$ the families of central, piecewise syndetic, dynamically piecewise syndetic, and dynamically central piecewise syndetic sets, respectively.  The following inclusions hold:
    \[
        \mathcal{C} \subsetneq dc\mathcal{PS} \subsetneq d\mathcal{PS} = \mathcal{PS}.
    \]
    In particular, a set is dynamically piecewise syndetic if and only if it is piecewise syndetic.
